candidates.exact_span: permittee must collect an effluent composite sample volume during the period of discharge that is sufficient to complete the required toxicity tests with daily renewal of effluent, and must meet the holding time between collection and first use of the sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sample volume, collection timing relative to discharge, daily renewal, and holding-time requirements were met affects whether toxicity monitoring was required and properly performed (B) and whether reported toxicity results constitute adequate evidence versus a missing or procedurally deficient result (C).

candidates.exact_span: When possible, the effluent samples used for the toxicity tests shall be collected on separate days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting 'when possible' and whether separate-day collection was required or satisfied changes whether the toxicity monitoring obligation was applicable/fulfilled (B) and whether a single-day collection must be treated as acceptable evidence or a deficiency (C).

candidates.exact_span: The effluent composite sample collection duration and the static renewal protocol associated with the abbreviated sample collection must be documented in the full report required in Item 3 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether documentation of collection duration and abbreviated static-renewal protocol is required evidence affects monitoring-obligation fulfillment (B) and whether missing documentation is a documented no-data state, other no-data state, or inadequate evidence for toxicity results (C).

candidates.exact_span: Test failure may not be construed or reported as invalid due to a coefficient of variation value of greater than 40%, or a PMSD value greater than the higher value on the range provided.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of this invalidity carve-out changes whether a toxicity test failure remains an enforceable compliance result for limit comparison (A), whether the monitoring event counts as completed/required (B), and whether high CV/PMSD should be classified as invalid/missing evidence versus a valid failed result (C).

candidates.exact_span: The statistical analyses used to determine if there is a significant difference between the control and the critical dilution shall be in accordance with the methods for determining the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) as described in the appropriate method manual listed in Part II or the most recent update thereof.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which NOEC method manual/version applies and how significance is determined can change the derived pass/fail or numeric endpoint used for compliance comparison (A) and whether a reported toxicity outcome is adequately supported versus unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Dilution water used in the toxicity tests will be receiving water collected as close to the point of discharge as possible but unaffected by the discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting proximity and 'unaffected by the discharge' affects whether the correct dilution water protocol was required and followed (B) and whether resulting toxicity data are valid evidence or must be treated as procedurally deficient/unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall substitute synthetic dilution water of similar pH, hardness, and alkalinity to the closest downstream perennial water for; i. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges to receiving water classified as intermittent streams; and ii. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether discharge occurred to intermittent streams or under zero-flow conditions triggers mandatory synthetic dilution water use, changing which monitoring protocol applies (B) and how to classify periods with no usable receiving water (documented no-discharge/conditional not required versus missing evidence) (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable receiving water test met the following stipulations: i. a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance requirements was run concurrently with the receiving water control; ii. the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to completion, iii. the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity with the full report and information required; and iv. the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Satisfaction of each substitution stipulation determines whether subsequent synthetic-dilution tests are valid for compliance determination (A), whether monitoring remained required after receiving-water failure (B), and whether absent concurrent controls, incomplete tests, or missing report inclusion must be treated as missing evidence versus acceptable conditional monitoring (C).
